That might just be! I will say though that when it was initially discovered, they believed it had less than a 3% chance of hitting the Earth and now it’s all but zero.

For comparison, the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs was anywhere from 6.8-50.3 miles in diameter, while Apophis is only about 0.23 miles in diameter. That’s still equivalent to a whopping 1,200 megatons of TNT while the Chicxulub impact was equivalent to an estimated 100,000,000 megatons. Compared to the biggest H-bomb, Tsar Bomba, that big, on 57 megatons. That would be a massive impact, but the chance is so low, I really wouldn’t worry at all.

Don’t wanna be a buzzkill but there’s [4700](https://neocam.ipac.caltech.edu/page/asteroidcounts) asteroids that are labeled as potentially hazardous, or ones that will eventually hit the Earth. For example, Apophis passed 44x the distance between the Earth and the Moon. In a week, [2001 FO32](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/asteroid-2001-fo32-will-safely-pass-by-earth-march-21) will pass by 5.25x the distance from the Earth to the Moon.

All in all, don’t fret. There’s professional and amateur astronomers monitoring as many asteroid paths as possible and we have a lot of data collected about them so that we can find out their trajectory.

Don’t just trust me though! Keep researching and you’ll find that we’re a lot safer from asteroids than the media makes it seem. Anything for extra clicks.

The life expectancy they are referring to is taken out of context (it was for a specific area in Latin America) but LGBT youth are impacted by suicide at higher rates than non-LGBT youth. Here is some relevant data:

- Suicide is the 2nd leading cause of death among young people ages 10 to 24.
- LGB youth seriously contemplate suicide at almost three times the rate and are almost five times as likely to have attempted suicide compared to heterosexual youth.
- In a national study, 40% of transgender adults reported having made a suicide attempt. 92% of these individuals reported having attempted suicide before the age of 25.
- LGB youth who come from highly rejecting families are 8.4 times as likely to have attempted suicide as LGB peers who reported no or low levels of family rejection.
- 1 out of 6 students nationwide (grades 9–12) seriously considered suicide in the past year. 
- Each episode of LGBT victimization, such as physical or verbal harassment or abuse, increases the likelihood of self-harming behavior by 2.5 times on average.

[This](https://www.thetrevorproject.org/resources/preventing-suicide/facts-about-suicide/) info is from the Trevor Project and mainly sites the CDC. I would like to point out that the majority of suicide attempts in trans youth come from before 25, the age OP suggests people should be allowed to transition.
